dataset: Gauthier, Dictionnaire des noms géographiques (DNG), t. 1-6: entries from the OCR text layer
work: Gauthier, Henri, Dictionnaire des noms géographiques contenus dans les textes hiéroglyphiques, tomes 1-6, Société royale de géographie d'Égypte (printed by IFAO), Le Caire (t. 1-2 1925, 3 1926, 4 1927, 5 1928, 6 1929)
rights: US public domain: HathiTrust records v. 1-6 as public domain in the US (Gauthier d. 1950). T. 7 (1931, the index) is not held.
scans: archive.org Gauthier1925_1 ... Gauthier1929 (Bordeaux Montaigne scans), each PDF with its OCR text layer; the _djvu.txt beside each carries the same OCR and is not read.

t1.page_rule: left half = 2 x pdf page - 14, right half = left + 1

t2.page_rule: left half = 2 x pdf page - 8, right half = left + 1

t3.page_rule: left half = 2 x pdf page - 8, right half = left + 1

t4.page_rule: left half = 2 x pdf page - 8, right half = left + 1

t5.page_rule: left half = 2 x pdf page - 8, right half = left + 1

t6.page_rule: left half = 2 x pdf page - 8, right half = left + 1

identity_rule: gauthier:t<volume>:p<printed page>:<n>, n the entry's place among the entries that open on that page (an entry runs on to later pages under the page it opens on; page_end gives the last). A rebuild that drops an id is refused unless --allow-drop names it (or is given bare, for every id); one that gives an id another kind or transcription is refused unless --allow-remap names it (ingest_guard.refuse_remapped on (kind, transcription)).
page_rule: pdf pages are two-page spreads; the printed page of each half is a constant offset per volume (sources.t<n>.page_rule). page_check compares it with the running-head folio and the sheet signature ('Dictionnaire, t. I. 3' opens p. 17, sheets of 8 pages) wherever the OCR reads one, and lists each disagreement.
split_rule: words are grouped into baseline rows (a word taller than 1.5 median heights, a hieroglyph group, joins the row whose foot is nearest its own; capitals of a heading stay words); the running head, the thumb letter above it and the signature line are dropped. The indent of a half page is the commonest left edge (3 pt bins) of its rows of four words or more. A row 24 pt or more left of it stands at the margin and opens an entry unless it reads as a line of the text with a stray mark before it (first word French, a French word after it with no citation near, a parenthesis of the text, the tail of a citation carried over); a row 8-24 pt left of it opens one only as a headword row (strays, then a transcription word with a citation or a comma close after). A margin row of strays alone is held and opens an entry with the next row when that row opens one or reads as a headword row. Every other row continues the open entry, across pages. In the addenda, set with first-line indents, a row 8-30 pt right of the half page's left edge opens an item, and so does the row after a heading. Flags: start_near_indent (opened 8-24 pt left of the indent), margin_row_continued (a margin row was read as a line of this entry: a start may have been missed), indent_from_volume (too few rows for the half's own indent; the volume's median for its side was used).
field_rule: transcription: the first run of transcription-like words (letters with the marks the OCR leaves inside one, a lower-case vowel, opening in lower case or as the OCR's ḥ: l;l l). J:i I:i Q.; a capitalised people or place is flagged headword_capitalised) before the first source citation, after the stray characters, up to a comma or a French word; strays glued to its front are cut (headword_glued_strays_stripped). key: ane_keys.loose_key of it. sources_cited: each (...) group of the head (the text before the dash that opens the description) that reads as a citation. gloss_fr: the head after the last citation when it reads as French, guillemets as the OCR gives them. description_fr: the text after that dash, dashes written —. identification_text: the dash-separated statements of the description naming a modern place, site or identification (actuel, aujourd'hui, moudirieh, markaz, identifié, correspond, Kôm, Tell, village, site ...). nome: each '<roman> nome de Haute-/Basse-Égypte' of the entry, in order; the first need not be the entry's own. variants: further transcriptions in the head (head_spelling) and each 'var.' statement. kind: cross_reference when the description is one short 'Voir ...' statement (see_text), addendum for the items of the Additions et corrections (addendum_to: the volume and page they correct), entry otherwise. All text is the OCR's, uncorrected.
join_rule: none: no row is joined to Trismegistos, Pleiades, PNM or any other layer, and no id is asserted.
override_rule: overrides.json {"entries": {id: {field: value, "basis": ...}}} fixes fields by id, each change kept in the row's corrections with its basis; a fixed transcription carries its key. The source facts (id, volume, page, pdf_page, raw_text ...) cannot be fixed.

export.rows: each row as the private build wrote it, without source_id
export.manifest: private catalogue ids, local paths (a path is given as its file name) and build-trail keys removed; outputs rehashed
